city.caveat: This is the official city record as kept, without adjustments. It joins several observing sites over the years, and a move, a new instrument or the city growing around a station can shift readings (city growth mostly warms nights); NOAA's adjusted climate datasets correct for these. Treat any single number as approximate.

text.t_rec: Wilmington is setting record highs far faster than chance
text.p_rec: If Wilmington's climate weren't changing, every year would have the same chance of holding a daily record. Since 2000, Wilmington has set 41 standing record lows, fewer than the 64 that chance alone would give, and 108 record highs, far more than the 64 that chance alone would give. The 2010s hold the most record highs of any decade (46). Wilmington's all-time high is 104°F, on June 27, 1952.
text.t_chg: Wilmington's nights have warmed since 1986. Its days have warmed.
text.p_chg: Across 151 complete years: Wilmington's average low shows no clear change: −0.04°F per decade, a range (−0.09 to +0.01) that includes zero. It's close, but the range still includes zero. Wilmington's average high has risen +0.24°F per decade (95% range +0.20 to +0.28), about +3.6°F since 1875. The last 40 years tell a different story: since 1986, lows have risen +0.58°F per decade (95% range +0.29 to +0.87) and highs have risen +0.38°F per decade (95% range +0.05 to +0.71). The full record joins different observing sites over the years, and a move (for example, from the city to a cooler airport) can hide or exaggerate a long-run trend, so the recent decades are the clearer guide here.
text.t_mon: Lows rose in 2 of 12 months; January fell. Highs rose in 11 of 12 months.
text.p_rain: Wilmington's yearly precipitation has risen +0.73 inches per decade (95% range +0.37 to +1.09), about +11.2 inches since 1871. The 1991–2020 normal is 60.1 inches a year. The wettest year was 2018 (102.40 in); the driest, 1909 (27.68 in).
